source: VGC: Fortnite Pirate Shop Token guide (published Nov 5, 2026, updated Nov 8 with Epic's confirmed odds)
text:
If you’re just finding out about this now, Pirate Shop Tokens were added to Fortnite as part of its current mini-season, Fortnite Treasure Hunters, which started on November 1.
The season is set to end on December 5, meaning it will only last for around a month, which makes finding a Pirate Shop Token even more stressful.
Throughout the season, a Treasure Hunt feature has been added to Battle Royale mode, where every time you open or break a chest, there’s a small chance that you’ll get a treasure reward.
One of the rarest of these rewards is what players are calling a Pirate Token, which gives access to the Pirate Shop.
If you’re lucky enough to find it, you’ll actually receive two tokens – one which can be activated at any point in 2026 between November 1 and December 15, and one which can be activated at any point in 2027 between January 1 and December.
When you activate a token, every single item in the Fortnite Shop which costs V-Bucks becomes entirely free for the next 14 days.
The only catches are you can’t claim Battle Pass levels, you can’t get bundles that cost real money (instead of V-Bucks), you can’t gift items to other players, and you can only claim one free sidekick.
Everything else – skins, emotes, backpacks, pickaxes, instruments, cars, gliders, jam tracks – is entirely free for you to claim, as if you were buying it with V-Bucks.
The good news is that everyone who plays Fortnite has an equal chance of finding a Pirate Shop Token. The bad news is there’s a big random element to it.
To find one, you have to open chests during Battle Royale and Zero Build modes. This can be any type of chest, including:
- Normal chests
- Rare chests
- Sprite Chests
- Buried Chests
- Wanted Poster Chests
- Relic Chests
Every time you open a chest, you have a slight chance of also getting a Treasure Hunt prize. This won’t come out of the chest like the usual weapons and other items, so you won’t have to pick it up – you’ll just get a message on the screen telling you what you got.
Treasure Hunt prizes are split into three tiers – Standard, Major and Supreme. If it’s standard you’ll get either a Sprite Locator, Lucky Locator, Golden Firework, Extraction Accelerator or Portable Extractor.
If it’s Major you’ll get one of the current week’s special cosmetics, which at the time of writing include a Mercedes AMG truck and A$AP Rocky’s solid gold Gauntlets. And if it’s Supreme, you’ll get one of two things – that week’s gold skin (currently the Solid Gold A$AP Rocky) or the Pirate Shop Token.
Every time you open a chest during a normal match, these are your odds of getting one of the treasures:
- Weekly Gold Outfit – 1 in 1,562,500
- Pirate Shop Access – 1 in 137,500
- Weekly Vehicle & Decal – 1 in 7,813
- Weekly Pickaxe or Backbling – 1 in 568
- Weekly Jam Track – 1 in 391
- Weekly Loading Screen – 1 in 272
- Gizmo (any) – 1 in 127
These are all nonsense – according to Epic games, everyone has an equal chance of finding a Pirate Shop Token. There’s no such thing as a Token Compass, and the skin you choose has no effect on your odds – just focus on opening chests.
The main tip doing the rounds is to play in a Squad. If you don’t have friends to play with you, just choose the Fill option to add random players to your squad of four.
The reason for this is that if anyone in your Squad finds the Pirate Shop Token in a chest, every member of the Squad gets it. This technically means that in each round you’re opening four times as many chests as usual.
